reply: Down here on the right side, low down. It started last night, about ten o'clock. So maybe fourteen hours.

utterance: Right, fourteen hours of pain low on the right side. A couple more questions: when it first started last night, was the pain in the same spot, or did it start somewhere else and move? And how would you describe it — a dull ache, a cramping pain, or sharp?
reply: It actually started around my belly button. It moved down to the right sometime overnight.

utterance: That's a really important detail. Now, how would you describe the pain itself — is it a dull ache or a sharp, stabbing pain? And on a scale of zero to ten, how bad is it right now? Does anything make it worse — like moving around, coughing, or the bumps in the car on the way here?

utterance: Samuel, I want to be straight with you: everything points to appendicitis — that's an inflamed appendix. The way your pain started around your belly button and moved to the right lower side, the fever, feeling sick and going off your food, and what I found when I pressed on your tummy all fit that picture. This isn't something that will settle at home — it needs to be dealt with in hospital today, most likely with an operation to remove the appendix. I'm going to arrange an ambulance to take you to the emergency department now, and I'll phone ahead so they're expecting you.
reply: An ambulance? Can't I just drive there myself?

awards.label: Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment

utterance: I hear you, but I'd really advise against driving. Your tummy showed signs of irritation of the abdominal lining — that means things could worsen quickly, and being in severe pain behind the wheel isn't safe for you or anyone else. The ambulance crew can look after you on the way and get you straight in. A couple of important things while we wait: don't eat or drink anything from now on, because if you need an operation your stomach needs to be empty — small sips of water to swallow a tablet are okay. Let me give you some paracetamol now for the pain, and I'll call the hospital to hand over your details.

awards.label: Phone the emergency department with a handover

utterance: At the hospital they'll take some blood tests, may do a scan of your tummy, and the surgeons will assess you — most likely they'll recommend an operation today to remove the appendix, usually with keyhole surgery. It's a very common operation and people your age generally recover quickly. The reason we're not mucking around is that an inflamed appendix can burst, and that turns a straightforward problem into a much more serious one — so please don't delay or try to tough it out. Do you have any questions for me? Is there someone — family or a mate — you'd like me to help you call to meet you at the hospital?
reply: Nah, I'll just ring my old man.
